prize_parts.citation: for the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep Pd-catalysed C-N coupling. Of the ten shortlisted candidacies it is the only one whose scientific case is fully settled: a new bond-forming reaction with a defined catalytic cycle, a rational ligand evolution (bidentate phosphines, then bulky biaryl phosphines and NHCs), more than 25 years of independent confirmation, and routine use in medicinal chemistry and process manufacture. Attribution is the cleanest on the table. Buchwald and Hartwig independently made the reaction general and practical, so two names cover it and the three-person limit does not bite. Round 1 showed that every other configuration needs an exclusion defended in public (Kondo/Nishida, Ciulli, Pappu/Mittag, Anderson/Langer, Kasianowicz/Branton). The Kosugi/Migita tin-amide work is real precedent but stoichiometric in tin and not a general catalytic method, and the citation wording 'ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed' handles that. I read the 2010 prize as honouring C-C bond formation; C-N coupling raises a different mechanistic problem (amine binding, deprotonation, difficult C-N reductive elimination) and needed its own ligands.
statement.case_against: Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize remains the main reservation, along with a further synthetic-methodology award in a field the Academy rewards often and the Kosugi priority question. I also have to note that my preference is isolated: the chair counts me as the only supporter, while three members prefer B006. Support counts do not settle the science, but I should weigh the possibility that colleagues see a newer modality as more pressing. I do not think the 2010 overlap is disqualifying, since C-N coupling solved a distinct problem. A fair reader could still call it a less novel idea than a new modality.

responses.point: Holds base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) first as the one clearly attributable invention with a stated chemical mechanism, with the broadest support and first clinical use, and notes that I ranked it eighth.
responses.response: I have reconsidered B006 and move it up to my first alternative. The adenine editor needing an evolved TadA is genuine new chemistry, and I accept that the 2020 prize honoured guided double-strand cleavage and not base conversion. I still do not move it to first place. Chabes, Zou and you all concede the Kondo/Nishida Target-AID priority problem against your own choice, and the three-person limit cannot resolve it without excluding an independent inventor. The clinical record is also only a few years old, with bystander and off-target questions open. A prize can wait for B006 to mature. It does not need to be this year's.

responses.point: Argues the 2020 prize honoured cleavage and not base conversion, and that the adenine editor is real new chemistry, so base editing is a distinct achievement.
responses.response: That answers the chair's first question for me: the increment over 2020 is real if the citation is written around deamination and not around genome editing. My objection is not novelty but timing and credit. By the same standard you apply to the 2020 prize, C-N coupling is distinct from the 2010 prize, since the bond and the mechanism differ. If distinctness from a prior prize is the test, B032 passes it as well as B006, and it adds a quarter-century of confirmation that B006 lacks. I would therefore ask you to weigh maturity as heavily as novelty.

responses.point: Prefers targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) as an induced-proximity design principle, citing the broadest placement across opening ballots as consensus-compatible.
responses.response: I agree B068 is chemically original and I keep it as an alternative. My concern remains the pairing. The heterobifunctional PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa) are separate discoveries with different lineages. You concede that no heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so the half you call most original still lacks clinical proof. The chair asks whether the third name should be Handa or Ciulli; I cannot see a defensible three-person cut that leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim or Gray. Broad placement across rankings shows acceptability, but it does not remove that attribution problem.

responses.point: Argues phase separation is a new organizing principle with a quantitative framework testable against experiment (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen).
responses.response: I share your standard that a prize should link theory to measurement, and Rosen's multivalency work does that in reconstituted systems. On the chair's question, I would not call the open in vivo status disqualifying in itself, since it is a normal open question in a young field. But I weigh it against the Pappu and Mittag exclusion and against the fact that few synthetic or physical-organic chemists would yet say condensates have changed their daily practice. C-N coupling has that daily-use record, which is why I rank B056 below my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which is my main concern and which I treat as a judgement of the chemistry and not a count.
How much weight the Kosugi/Migita precedent should carry, and whether the 'ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed' wording is enough.
Whether the committee will prefer the base editing case on novelty (Chabes, Zou) over maturity, and whether Target-AID inclusion can be resolved within three names.
Whether my position is shaped by my synthetic-chemistry background and so underweights the medical consequences of the chemical-biology candidates.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen since round 1. Hartwig and Buchwald have no connection to Lund, KTH, Chalmers, Tartu or my mentor Masamune, none of the other credited names on my alternatives are personal collaborators, and I do not request recusal. I note again that I use their methods as a synthetic chemist and that I share a Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr, which is a connection among colleagues and not to any candidate.
